sections.heading: What is the subjunctive?
sections.body:
So far you've used the **indicative**: verb forms that state facts (*Ana viene* — Ana is coming). The **subjunctive** (*el subjuntivo*) is a second set of forms used when the speaker is *not* simply stating a fact: wishing, wanting, feeling, doubting, or talking about something not yet real. *Quiero que Ana venga.* (I want Ana to come.)

It appears mostly after *que* in a second clause, triggered by the first clause. English barely has it ("I suggest that he **be** there"), but in Spanish it's everywhere — this whole level is about when to use it.

sections.heading: Forming the present subjunctive
sections.body: Start from the *yo* form of the present indicative, drop the *-o*, and add the "opposite" vowel endings: *-ar* verbs take *e*, *-er / -ir* verbs take *a*. You already know most of these forms from the *usted* commands!

sections.heading: The yo-form rule gives you the irregulars for free
sections.body:
Because it starts from *yo*, any irregularity in the *yo* form carries through: *tengo → tenga*, *hago → haga*, *pongo → ponga*, *salgo → salga*, *digo → diga*, *vengo → venga*, *conozco → conozca*, *veo → vea*, *traigo → traiga*.

Spelling changes keep the sound: *buscar → busque*, *llegar → llegue*, *empezar → empiece*, *pagar → pague*, *escoger → escoja* (to choose). (Avoid *coger* in most of Latin America — there it's a vulgar word; say *tomar* or *agarrar* for "to take / grab".)

Notice *yo* and *él/ella/usted* are identical: *que yo hable, que ella hable*.

examples: Quiero que Ana venga a la fiesta.
I want Ana to come to the party.
Necesito que me ayudes.
I need you to help me.
Quiero que hables con él.
I want you to talk to him.
Mis padres quieren que yo estudie más.
My parents want me to study more.
Necesito que llegues temprano.
I need you to arrive early.
Quiero que comamos juntos.
I want us to eat together.
Necesitamos que ustedes vivan cerca.
We need you all to live nearby.
Quiero que me digas la verdad.
I want you to tell me the truth.
Necesito que hagas la tarea.
I need you to do your homework.
Quiero que tengas cuidado.
I want you to be careful.
El profesor quiere que leamos el libro.
The teacher wants us to read the book.
Necesito que pongas la mesa.
I need you to set the table.
Quiero que conozcas a mi familia.
I want you to meet my family.
No quiero que salgas tan tarde.
I don't want you to go out so late.
Quiero que paguen hoy.
I want them to pay today.
Necesito que me traigas el libro.
I need you to bring me the book.
Quiero estudiar, pero quiero que tú estudies también.
I want to study, but I want you to study too.

exercises.prompt: The present subjunctive is built from…
options: the yo form of the present, minus -o

exercises.prompt: -ar verbs take which vowel in the subjunctive?
The subjunctive of *tener* (él) is…
Which is correct: "I want you to go out"?
"I want to go" (same subject) is…
exercises.explain: Same person wanting and doing → infinitive. Different people → *que* + subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: The subjunctive of *buscar* (yo) is…
I want you to help me. (tú)
I need you to arrive early. (tú)
My parents want me to study more.
answers: Mis padres quieren que estudie más.
Mis padres quieren que yo estudie más.
